draft.title: Reading chemical formulas
card: A chemical formula shows which atoms are in a substance. It uses the symbol for each element.
A small number written after a symbol tells you how many atoms of that element there are. In H2O, the 2 means two hydrogen atoms.
If a symbol has no small number, there is one atom of that element. H2O has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
The small number only applies to the symbol just before it. In CO2, the 2 applies to O, so there is one carbon atom and two oxygen atoms.
draft.remember: Read each symbol, then the small number after it. No number means one atom.

a.q: What does the formula H2O tell you about one unit of water?
opts: It has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom
It has one hydrogen atom and two oxygen atoms
It has two hydrogen atoms and two oxygen atoms
It has one hydrogen atom and one oxygen atom
a.why: The small 2 comes after H, so it applies to hydrogen. O has no number, so there is one oxygen atom. Putting the 2 on oxygen reverses the formula.
a.clue: Which symbol sits directly before the small 2?

b.q: Ammonia has the formula NH3. How many atoms of each element are in one unit of ammonia?
opts: One nitrogen atom and three hydrogen atoms
Three nitrogen atoms and one hydrogen atom
One nitrogen atom and one hydrogen atom
Three nitrogen atoms and three hydrogen atoms
b.why: The small 3 comes after H, so there are three hydrogen atoms. N has no number, so there is one nitrogen atom. The 3 does not apply to N, which is the tempting mistake.
b.clue: The small number applies only to the symbol just before it.

a.best: It has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom

b.best: One nitrogen atom and three hydrogen atoms
